title: Construct Binary Search Tree from Preorder Traversal
prompt:
Given an array `preorder` representing the pre-order traversal of a binary search tree, reconstruct the tree and return it.

It is guaranteed that there is always a unique binary search tree that results in the given pre-order traversal. Since this is a coding exercise rather than an interactive class-based design, the function returns the rebuilt tree serialized to a level-order array (`null` for missing children, the standard LeetCode serialization) using the provided `tree_to_level_order` helper.

examples.explanation: 8 is the root; values less than 8 (5,1,7) form the left subtree, values greater (10,12) form the right subtree, recursively.

constraints: All values of preorder are unique
hints: Unlike the general 'construct from preorder and inorder' problem, here you don't need a second traversal — the BST property alone tells you which values belong in the left vs. right subtree.

The first value in preorder is always the root of the current subtree; every subsequent value less than it belongs in the left subtree, and every value greater belongs in the right subtree, both as contiguous runs (a BST's preorder groups all lesser values immediately after the root, before any greater values appear).

Recurse with an upper bound: build(bound) consumes values from a shared pointer into preorder as long as they're less than bound, first with bound = infinity for the left spine's boundary, and bound = parent's value when building a right subtree that must stay under an ancestor's constraint.

solution.approach: Use a recursive helper build(bound) that consumes preorder values (via a shared index) as long as they're less than the given upper bound, constructing a valid BST subtree. The root of each call is the next unconsumed preorder value; its left subtree is built with bound = the node's own value (since left descendants must be smaller), and its right subtree is built with the same bound inherited from the parent (since right descendants must still respect the ancestor constraint, just be larger than the current node — handled implicitly because we only stop consuming once we exceed bound). This exploits that in a BST's preorder, all left-subtree values appear as a contiguous block immediately after the root, before any right-subtree values.
